_comment: Storm Charge tuning. Portable balance data - no Roblox types in here. RETUNED 2026-10-26 to Chris's curve, replacing the handoff's 8-minutes-to-first-threshold anchor, which left a dark crew with no escalation inside any run it would actually play. One active lantern still raises the meter 2.5x - that anchor is untouched. One charge unit is one second of darkness.

lantern._comment: multiplier = 1 + perLanternBonus * (1 - diminishingDecay^activeLanterns) / (1 - diminishingDecay). One lantern = 2.5x, per the handoff, and the diminishing curve preserves that anchor exactly. Each further lantern adds less than the one before it but never nothing, so no keeper's light is free.
lantern._curveChoice: Chris, 2026-10-27: 'Switch storm-charge.json to the diminishing curve so no keeper's light is free.' This closes the question docs/VERTICAL-SLICE.md raised - under linearCapped a crew of three at 25% duty met the Warden at 5:31 and a fourth lantern cost nothing, so a four-player run was always the shortest one. Diminishing was already written and tested; only this line moved.
lantern._maxMultiplierNote: INERT while curve is 'diminishing' - that curve self-limits at 4.75x and needs no clamp. Kept because it is the clamp linearCapped would use if the curve were ever switched back, and because the balance test still checks a cap can never sit below the one-lantern anchor.

_curveOptions.linearCapped: 1 + bonus*n, hard-clamped at maxMultiplier. Simple, but every lantern past the clamp is free: three (5.5x) and four (7x) both clamp to 5.0. Was the default until 2026-10-27.
_curveOptions.diminishing: ACTIVE. 1 + bonus*(1-decay^n)/(1-decay). Each extra lantern adds less than the last but never nothing, so no player's light is free. Preserves the locked 2.5x one-lantern anchor exactly and self-limits near 4.75x with the values below - no clamp needed.

lantern._decayNote: Only used when curve is 'diminishing'. 0.6 gives 2.5 / 3.40 / 3.94 / 4.26 for one to four lanterns, asymptote 4.75.

_tuning: Chris, 2026-10-26, for a normal 10-12 minute run. Fully dark: first real pressure around minute 4-5, severe pressure near the final minutes. Lantern used regularly: first pressure around minute 2-3, serious pursuit around minute 6-7. 'So light is never an optional visual effect. It is how you see, find better loot, trigger certain enemies, and make the run escalate faster.'
_derivation: regularUseSeconds assumes the lantern lit about half the time, which is multiplier 1 + 1.5*0.5 = 1.75. At 270 / 480 / 700 that gives dark 4:30 / 8:00 / 11:40 and regular use 2:34 / 4:34 / 6:40, which hits all four of Chris's anchors. oneLanternSeconds is the constant-lit case at 2.5x and is a ceiling nobody plays, not a target. Verified with: node tests/pacing.mjs

run._comment: ADDED 2026-10-28. Run length had no home in the portable layer at all - it lived only in src/shared/Config.luau as the misnamed targetMaxSeconds, which is frozen Luau (row 33) and does not port. So the most-argued-about number in the project was unreadable by the Unreal build. These keys give it one, with the misnaming fixed: a ceiling is not a target, which is the whole of O1.
run._authority: Chris's own most recent numbers, not inferred. docs/GAME-THESIS.md: 'The first successful run should take roughly ten to twelve minutes.' docs/STEAM-PRODUCTION-PLAN.md locks a 10-12 minute department store expedition. This file's own _tuning line already said 'for a normal 10-12 minute run' on 2026-10-26.
run._supersedesO1: NEEDS CHRIS'S WORD. O1's table says the target run is 6-10 minutes; his thesis and production plan both say 10-12, and they are newer. Written here as 10-12 because it is his latest statement twice over, but the older 6-10 is still sitting in O1 and somebody has to retire one of them. Nothing else in the file depends on which wins - the thresholds were tuned against the 10-12 reading.
run._targetNote: 11 minutes, the midpoint of his 10-12. One raid is one night (row 48), so this is the night's window and the run length at once - they stopped being two numbers.
run._earlyExitNote: 5 minutes, the midpoint of O1's 'early exit ~4-6 min' for the loading dock. Reliable, pays less. Not restated anywhere newer, so O1 remains its only source.
run._hardCeilingNote: 20 minutes. A safety valve, never a goal, and deliberately NOT called targetMaxSeconds - that name is what made four sources disagree three ways for a week.

extractionCall._comment: Chris, 2026-10-26: 'Calling extraction: a deliberate loud spike - flare, siren, enemies converging - regardless of current Storm Charge.' Extraction is the climax, not a checkbox: the argument the run builds toward is 'we have enough - call the loud extraction now, defend it, or risk one more store?'
extractionCall._spikeNote: PROPOSED, Chris to set. 180 is three minutes of darkness applied at once, which is deliberately large against thresholds of 270 / 480 / 700 - calling it mid-run should move you a stage, so that calling early and calling late are different decisions. The anchor revive's spike is 120 for comparison.

thresholds.effect: Patrol routes tighten and Sweepers investigate noise further from their spawn.
All patrols actively hunt. Glimmer scan frequency increases.
The Warden spawns at the rooftop stage and converges on the crew's brightest position.

anchorRevive._comment: Solo rule: one self-revive per run, paid for with light.
anchorRevive._soloOnlyNote: LOCKED by the handoff: "Solo players receive one Anchor Revive per run." It exists so a lone Lightkeeper is not hard-wiped on a first knockdown. Granting it to a crew breaks the other half of the same rule - a whole crew down must wipe rather than wait indefinitely for someone to press R. Chris later locked the harsher haul rule: a wipe without extraction loses all run loot. Do not set false without changing the handoff first.
